resources.string: Apply to every game that does not change the same setting. %1$d away from the default.
Only for %1$s, on every disc and copy; the rest follows the global settings.
Apply to every game that does not change the same setting.
Every setting of %1$s went back to global
Also changes with the game open, from the in-game menu
No effect on Turnip: it lacks VK_EXT_external_memory_host.
Only with Force maximum GPU clocks on.
Written with an atomic swap; keys the app does not know stay intact.
Only what this game changes; the rest comes from the global config.
Only the lines away from the default; the whole file stays as it is.
The whole file has every key; the ones the app does not know stay intact.
Apply several settings to this game at once; you can undo.
FSR on the output and 4x anisotropic filtering.
2x scale, Lanczos and 16x anisotropic. Costs GPU time and memory.
Width reported to the game when the display mode is Custom. The core accepts 1 to 1920.
Height reported to the game when the display mode is Custom. The core accepts 1 to 1080.
Keep narrow surfaces at native size
With the resolution scale above 1x, surfaces up to this width stay at native size. Bloom and depth of field often break when upscaled; use the smallest value that fixes the effect.
Extra sharpening on top of CAS (Scaling & sharpening: cas); higher is sharper and may show halos.
How much FSR softens its sharpening (Scaling & sharpening: fsr); 0 is the sharpest, 2 the softest.
How many times FSR may upscale in a row when the screen is much larger than the game. More passes cost GPU time.
Display gamma reported to games. BT.709 is the closest to an Xbox 360 on an HDTV
Gamma exponent used when the gamma type is power (custom). The core\'s default is 2.22.
Keep at least this much of the width
When the picture would get bars at the sides or top, how much of its width must stay on screen; below 100 the edges may be cut instead of drawing bars.
Keep at least this much of the height
When the picture would get bars at the top or sides, how much of its height must stay on screen; below 100 the edges may be cut instead of drawing bars.
Creates shaders and pipelines on background threads: no stutter while a scene is new, but its first frames may miss an object. Off creates them on the spot: stutter, nothing missing.
Interpret vertex shaders while they compile
Draws new vertex shaders with the interpreter until their compiled version is ready, instead of stalling on the translation.
Skip draws until the shader is ready
Skips draws whose shader cannot be used yet (tessellation, for one) until it compiles in the background. Avoids stutter; the geometry shows up a few frames later.
Create stored pipelines when a game starts
Creates, when a game starts, the pipelines earlier sessions used, so they do not compile mid-game. Off still reuses the stored shaders.
Keeps translated shaders and loads them when the game starts again, so a second session stutters less
Serves the game\'s waits with sub-millisecond accuracy. A plain system sleep overshoots and lengthens every frame.
Registers an ADPF performance hint session over the dispatch and audio threads so the system holds clocks for the audio deadline.
Force the GPU to its maximum clocks via the custom driver; more speed, more heat and battery drain.
The max-clocks request is lost when the app leaves the foreground; this asks again every this many seconds after resuming. 0 asks only at start. Needs Force max GPU clocks.
Threads that create pipelines in the background. 0 creates them on the spot
Submit to the GPU every N draws
Submit GPU work after this many draws instead of once per frame; 0 off, too low hurts tiled GPUs.
Run guest threads as cooperative fibers on a few host threads instead of one thread each; takes effect next launch.
Volume of all audio output. The in-game menu still changes it live; this is the starting value.
How much audio the device buffers ahead. Lower means less audio delay; too low and audio breaks up on slower devices.
After audio breaks up, buffer one step more (up to three times the depth above); after 30 s without a break, one step less. Fewer dropouts in slow scenes, the chosen delay otherwise.
Which XMA audio decoder to use, trading stability against legacy Xenia behavior.
Turns the vibration a game asks for on or off.
Send the Guide button to the game
Forwards Guide button presses to the game.
Makes GPU writes the game reads back visible. Fixes missing models in Team Ninja games. Costs a pass per frame: use it per game
Convert float24 depth in the pixel shader
Avoids GPU hangs (device lost) on Adreno with Turnip in some games, such as Ninja Gaiden II
How visibility queries (lens flares, culling, auto-exposure) are answered: faked, async, or exact.
Waits for the GPU after each copy to the game\'s memory so it is coherent in the same frame. Off copies without waiting.
Interpolates pixel shader inputs exactly as the console does. Fixes noise in games such as Perfect Dark and Tenchu Z. Needs barycentrics in the driver (VK_KHR_fragment_shader_barycentric).
Avoids Z-fighting in games that rely on tiny depth bias values. Small cost.
Which resolves are copied back to guest RAM; UMA reads mapped memory directly and is the only mode that works on Adreno.
Memory export visible to the CPU
Makes memory export output visible to the CPU, for games that read back what the GPU exported. No effect on Turnip, which lacks VK_EXT_external_memory_host.
Reverse depth straight to the driver
Passes reverse depth ranges (inverse-Z) directly to the driver. Turn off if the driver draws them wrong.
Hack for games with setjmp/longjmp problems.
Skips the real time of the game\'s wait loops. Turn off for a game that depends on that time
Comma-separated TU_DEBUG flags for the Turnip driver; e.g. sysmem disables tiled rendering (Turnip only).
Uses VK_KHR_dynamic_rendering instead of traditional render passes. May improve or worsen performance depending on the driver.
On tile-based GPUs (Adreno/Turnip), routes point sprites and quad lists through cheaper paths. Read when the GPU starts.
Uses the D24_UNORM_S8_UINT format when the driver supports it. Off forces the float32 emulation, as on Adreno\'s own driver.
Off, the achievement notification always shows at the bottom centre.
Executable on the disc or package to launch instead of default.xex. Blank uses the default.
Mounts a memory unit (MU) like the console\'s.
Console type reported to the game.
Extra command line for the game
Arguments handed to the game when it starts.
End when a game thread crashes
Writes a full report and ends the game, instead of leaving the thread stopped (which looks like a hang). Turn off only to inspect.
Applies installed title updates when launching a game.
Applies title updates even when their signature doesn\'t match the game.
Lets games see a network connection
Play System Link with the devices on the same Wi-Fi. Turn it on in each one, then pick the game\'s System Link mode. Halo 3 also needs its \"Allow public IP addresses.\" patch on
IP addresses of devices on another network or a VPN (ZeroTier, Tailscale), separated by commas
Which content licenses games see as owned: none, the first, or all (unlocks full versions of arcade games)
Video signal standard the console reports (NTSC, NTSC-J, or PAL); can affect region behavior.
Runs PAL games in 50Hz (PAL-50) mode instead of 60Hz.
Maximum log verbosity: 0 errors, 1 warnings, 2 info, 3 debug.
Which subsystems write to the log: everything, only one (GPU, audio, kernel or CPU), or all but one. Lines with no subsystem always stay; takes effect at the next start.
Show an on-screen overlay with FPS, frame times, and in-flight shader compiles.
How many past sessions\' log zips to keep in the logs folder before old ones are rotated out.
Search every setting, key or description
